top.title: 8 takeaways from the Bears' stressful win over the Buccaneers
top.description: The victories seemed to be coming a little too easy for the Chicago Bears in recent weeks, so they made sure to put everyone through an extremely stressful one before heading off for their bye week. The Bears wrapped up their three-game prime-time tour with a home matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football and escaped with a 27-24 victory and improved to 7-2 on the season. Early on, however, it felt as if the game would be a blowout. Quarterback Caleb Williams quickly led two scoring drives to put the Bears up 14-0, with Tampa seemingly having no answers on either side of the ball. Everything was looking great, but then Williams began turning the ball over, something that is rare for him. Williams threw a career-high four interceptions on the day, and the Bears had five turnovers on the day. The offense couldn't muster any momentum, putting all the pressure on the Bears defense, which came through multiple times. The defense couldn't hold their ground forever, though. Eventually, those offensive miscues helped Tampa get back into the game as the Bears blew a 24-13 lead early in the fourth quarter to be tied 24-24 with just under two minutes to play. Fortunately, Williams responded by putting together one last scoring drive, complete with a big 38-yard completion to Colston Loveland to put the Bears in field goal range. Cairo Santos drilled a game-winning kick as everyone collectively exhaled. This will be one of the more memorable wins for all the wrong reasons, but it's still a win that keeps the Bears near the top of the playoff picture. Here are our takeaways from Sunday's stressful victory: 1. This is the reincarnation of 2006's Miracle in the Desert 20 years ago, Bears fans were treated to one of the most improbable and ugly wins in a special season. That, of course, was the "Miracle in the Desert" comeback win against the Arizona Cardinals, where the Bears committed six turnovers and needed big plays from the defense and special teams to get back in the game. And though this game may not have had the same comeback theatrics, it was every bit as gross and gritty to keep the winning streak alive. For nearly three full quarters, the offense didn't do much of anything and needed to rely on big plays by the defense to pick up the slack. It was ugly, and everything that could go wrong did go wrong. But the Bears never gave up and dug deep to get this victory. And great teams need to do that every once in a while. The Miracle in the Desert proved to everyone in the locker room that they have what it takes to win, no matter what happens. And that mindset helped propel them to Super Bowl XLI. Hopefully this will do the same, especially since it's the first time the Bears have won a game with a -3 turnover differential since then. We'll look back on this game with fond memories when the Bears are gunning for a title. 2. Caleb Williams had his worst game in 2 years This was a game we've quite literally never seen from Williams.

top.title: Harry Kane left out of FIFPRO World 11 team as Messi returns
top.description: Harry Kane left out of FIFPRO World 11 team as Messi returns Lionel Messi has extended his record number of FIFPRO World 11 appearances to 18, while Lucy Bronze has set a new women’s record after being selected for the ninth time. More than 26,000 professional footballers from 75 countries voted for the 2026 men’s and women’s teams. Messi returns to the team for the first time since 2023 and is joined in the men’s XI by the likes of Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Though there is no place for Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. Yamal has also made history by becoming the first player to earn two World 11 selections before turning 20. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is selected after helping Spain win the 2026 World Cup, with compatriots Pau Cubarsi and Rodri also included. Jude Bellingham is the only English player in the men’s side, while Paris Saint-Germain trio Achraf Hakimi, Nuno Mendes and Vitinha are all recognised. In the women’s team, Bronze makes a record ninth appearance and is one of five England players selected. Chelsea goalkeeper Hannah Hampton, Manchester City defender Alex Greenwood, Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone and Arsenal striker Alessia Russo also make the XI. Barbra Banda is the only player in the women’s team from outside England or Spain, with the Zambia forward earning her third selection. 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11 Goalkeeper: David Raya (Arsenal, Spain) Defenders: Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona, Spain), Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain, Morocco), Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Midfielders: Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid, England), Rodri (Manchester City/Barcelona, Spain), Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Forwards: Erling Haaland (Manchester City, Norway), Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid, France), Lionel Messi (Inter Miami, Argentina), Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, Spain) 2026 FIFPRO Women’s World 11 Goalkeeper: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea, England) Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea, England), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City, England), Mapi Leon (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Irene Paredes (Barcelona, Spain) Midfielders: Aitana Bonmati (Barcelona, Spain), Alexia Putellas (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Ella Toone (Manchester United, England) Forwards: Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride, Zambia), Claudia Pina (Barcelona, Spain), Alessia Russo (Arsenal, England) The men’s voting was based on performances between August 4, 2025 and July 19, 2026, while the women’s voting period ran until August 16. Players selected the three footballers they believed had performed best in each position, with the highest-ranked players forming the final World 11.

top.title: Dan Campbell Has Complicated Decision to Make Before Germany Game
top.description: The Detroit Lions improved to 6-2 with Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins, but head coach Dan Campbell now has an interesting decision to make regarding his offensive line. And based on what happened in Miami, it might be a decision that is easier to make on paper than in the locker room. Christian Mahogany was surprisingly benched for violating team rules, opening the door for second-year offensive lineman Miles Frazier to make his first NFL start at left guard. Unfortunately for Detroit, the results weren’t exactly encouraging. Campbell has built his program around accountability, and that’s not something he should abandon. However, with the Lions preparing for another important matchup against the New England Patriots, the question becomes whether Mahogany has already served his punishment or whether Campbell intends to make a longer-term change. His 48.8 pass-blocking grade and team-worst 37.8 run-blocking grade certainly won’t help his argument for remaining in the starting lineup. top.title: ‘There was some deli meat given out’: Tom Brady takes jab at Drake Maye
top.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Tom Brady returned to Foxboro this weekend for Rob Gronkowski’s New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction Saturday and Sunday’s game between the Pats and the Green Bay Packers. The former event went swimmingly for New England fans; the latter less so. Led by Jordan Love’s 372 passing yards and four total touchdowns, the Packers routed the Patriots 45-27. Drake Maye, New England’s third-year quarterback, had his share of struggles, tossing three critical interceptions. After the game, Brady the broadcaster had some fun at Maye’s expense during FOX’s postgame interviews. Drake throwing ‘deli meat’ Speaking with Green Bay Packers safety Evan Williams (five tackles, one interception), Brady noted that Maye was being generous with his passes throughout the game. “Xavier [McKinney] had two picks, you had one on the sideline. There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today,” Brady said . “I’m not gonna say that,” Williams responded, laughing, “but he was giving us some gifts for sure.” “There was a few out there, and you made him pay,” Brady added. Tom Brady took a dig at Drake Maye while interviewing #Packers S Evan Williams: “There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today.” ( @NFLonFOX) https://t.co/qp4SfQj1qP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 9, 2026 If you’re unfamiliar, Brady’s “deli meat” reference is a nod to Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake, who said last week that struggling Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was “throwing deli meat out there” in a loss to the Rams. Lake later apologized to Herbert via text message, claiming he wasn’t trying to be “disrespectful.” Back to Brady We’re guessing Brady wasn’t trying to be cruel toward Maye with his postgame barb, even if his assessment was harsh (though not unfair). After throwing only four touchdowns and seven interceptions in his first four games, Maye tossed 11 TDs and only one pick his next four before Sunday’s ugly showing. “We haven’t had a clean, a turnover-free game yet. It’s, starting with me, it’s one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games,” Maye said after yesterday’s loss. “I’d say, put our defense in a bad spot in the first, the first drive, and just gave them the football and had some other chances down the field and got to see in front. I got to see in front. I feel like I was just a little late sometimes. I feel like we got into a throwing game, and that’s partly because of what we did offensively, and then we didn’t really get to build off the run game, and I think we just got to start the game, and me specifically, start better.” New England is back in action this Sunday when they take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany. The apex socio-political organisation of the South-South region also called for an immediate end to political violence, intimidation and thuggery, warning that such activities were alien to the values and traditions of peaceful coexistence in the region. PANDEF made the call in a statement issued on Monday and signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali. The organisation expressed concern over the incidents, particularly the reported loss of life in Asaba, and described the violence as a threat to peaceful coexistence in the Niger Delta. It specifically cited incidents in the Warri/Effurun axis on September 18, 2026; Calabar on November 4; and Asaba on November 7, 2026. The statement read: “The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) notes with very serious concern and strongly condemns the disturbing incidents of political violence recorded around our region. Most worrisome are the sad events which occurred in the Warri/Effurun axis on Friday, 18th September 2026; in Calabar on Wednesday, 4th November, 2026 and most recently, the incident in Asaba on Saturday, 7th November 2026 in which a life was lost! “Indeed, as the mother body of the peoples of the region, PANDEF views these developments as a sacrilege to our peaceful co-existence in the Niger Delta and strongly condemns them.” Igali said peaceful coexistence, tolerance and political forbearance were values inherited from the region’s founding fathers and must be preserved. He urged political leaders, party supporters and other stakeholders to demonstrate maturity and embrace sportsmanship in resolving political disagreements. The forum also warned political leaders against inflammatory rhetoric, provocation and actions capable of triggering violence, stressing that they had a responsibility to guide their followers. PANDEF particularly appealed to youths in the Niger Delta not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, intimidation or thuggery. top.title: TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress Banks will try again to stop crypto platforms from paying yield on stablecoin balances, but TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg puts only a 10% chance on Congress enacting such a ban over the next two years, he wrote in a Monday policy note shared with Bitcoin Magazine and clients. The issue is whether exchanges and other platforms can offer yield or rewards to investors who keep dollar-pegged stablecoins on their platforms. Seiberg views action as unlikely, though he sees a “narrow path” for a ban. His rationale is procedural as much as political: it may be easier to find 60 Senate votes on stablecoin yield alone than on the broader crypto market structure bill, which failed a cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and which he already called effectively dead for this Congress after the Democratic midterm sweep. A ban, he wrote, would benefit banks. He expects them to renew the push in the next Congress on the theory that Democratic wins open a path. Why Seiberg still sees a path That path rests on a shift in the Senate. Key crypto advocates retired or lost, while skeptics are being elevated. Sen. Elizabeth Warren is likely to chair the Banking Committee, and Sen. Sherrod Brown, a longtime critic of the industry, regained his Ohio seat after crypto-backed spending of about $64 million failed to stop him, Seiberg wrote before the votes were counted. It is not his base case. Crypto politics are “complex,” he wrote, which is why the probability starts at 10%. Some Democrats will resist treating stablecoin yield outside a broader package. Seiberg again sees no path for the Clarity Act, arguing Democrats will insist on ethics and investor-protection provisions President Trump would reject. That split, he wrote, makes Democrats unlikely to unite behind a yield-only bill. Democrats are not united on the substance either. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, a lead Democrat on crypto policy, has backed paying rewards for using stablecoins rather than for passively holding them, a distinction that shaped the Tillis-Alsobrooks compromise text during Clarity talks. There is also a perception problem. Congress would be asked to stop voters from earning a return on stablecoin holdings even though they can earn one on savings accounts and money market funds. Seiberg questions whether Democratic leaders want a vote that could be framed as taking money from retail investors. What GENIUS already banned, and what it left open The fight is leftover business from the GENIUS Act, which President Trump signed on July 18, 2025, as Public Law 119-27. The statute bars permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers from paying “any form of interest or yield” solely for holding, using or retaining a payment stablecoin. top.title: Nvidia’s board needs to do some succession planning – sharpish | Nils Pratley
top.description: The chipmaker faces business risks and political scrutiny due to its over-reliance on founder and CEO Jensen Huang Why is Nvidia’s Jensen Huang at the centre of a US-China row? Too big – and too well-connected – to sack? One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to think Jensen Huang, the Nvidia boss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation into the alleged honeytrap spy scandal . The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power. Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying about succession planning and “key person risk” or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US. nigeria.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has said the administration of President Bola Tinubu is driving economic growth and improving security in the South-East through investments in road infrastructure, agriculture, renewable energy, housing and human capital development. Shettima said the Federal Government’s interventions in Ebonyi State and the wider South-East were aimed at improving regional connectivity, strengthening food security, expanding economic opportunities and addressing longstanding development challenges. The Vice-President spoke on Monday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, where he urged residents to renew Tinubu’s mandate in the 2027 general elections. He said the administration had demonstrated its commitment to Ebonyi through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and policies designed to improve citizens’ welfare. “This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have triumphed over those who mistook the limits of their imagination for the limits of our reach. “We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects and His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state,” he said. Shettima described public office as a responsibility to deliver measurable improvements in the lives of citizens, adding that the administration was seeking another mandate to consolidate its development programmes. “If any state can speak with confidence about the dividends of democracy, it is Ebonyi. You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. “We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, to defend you, and to stand by you,” he said. Highlighting federal infrastructure investments, the Vice-President listed the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway as one of the major projects expected to strengthen trade and economic integration between the South-East, North-Central and other parts of the country. He also mentioned the Ndibe Bridge, which is designed to connect Ebonyi with Cross River State, as well as ongoing work on the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. According to him, the projects will ease the movement of agricultural produce, manufactured goods and other commodities while reducing transportation challenges for businesses and communities. On agriculture, Shettima described Ebonyi as an important contributor to Nigeria’s food security, particularly in rice and cassava production. nigeria.title: Fani-Kayode urges South Africa to replace xenophobia with Pan-Africanism
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has called on South Africa to embrace Pan-Africanism and reject xenophobic sentiments that have fuelled attacks on Nigerians and other African nationals in the country. Fani-Kayode made the call on Saturday while speaking at the inaugural Nigerian Fair held at the Nigerian Consulate in Johannesburg. He recalled Nigeria’s contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa, stressing that the liberation movement was a collective African effort. “It wasn’t a black South African struggle. It was a struggle that every nation in Africa led primarily by the frontline states and Nigeria, and every decent civilized nation in the world supported,” he said. The high commissioner urged South Africans not to forget the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. He said Nigeria and the rest of Africa had a stake in South Africa’s development because of their contributions to the country’s liberation. Fani-Kayode described xenophobic attacks as a retrogressive sentiment, urging African countries to strengthen solidarity and cooperation. “We must understand that the world is coming together as one, and we must stand together as one,” he said. He claimed that Nigeria contributed no less than $61 billion to the anti-apartheid struggle between 1960 and 1994, adding that the country also deployed troops to frontline states in support of the campaign against the apartheid regime. He cited the introduction of the “Mandela Tax”, through which Nigerian civil servants contributed financially to the struggle, as one of the country’s solidarity measures. “Nigeria did so much. Mandela tax — we imposed a tax on our own civil servants during the course of the struggle, and that money was channelled to the ANC,” he said. He added that Nigerian schoolchildren also contributed their lunch money to support the struggle, while the country consistently advocated South Africa’s liberation at the United Nations and other international platforms. Fani-Kayode called for stronger ties between Nigeria and South Africa, urging both countries to build bridges of friendship, fraternity and mutual respect. He described perpetrators of xenophobic attacks as a minority driven by what he called Afrophobia and xenophobia. The high commissioner said Nigeria must continue to promote African unity and avoid actions that could further strain relations between the two countries. He also said Nigeria would not sever its economic ties with South Africa despite calls by some Nigerians for such a move, although he acknowledged that patience was wearing thin within the corridors of power. Fani-Kayode assured Nigerians living in South Africa that the Federal Government would continue to take steps to protect their interests and ensure their welfare. nigeria.title: ‘Student is alive’ – Babcock University clarifies viral hall incident
nigeria.description: Babcock University has confirmed that a student involved in an incident at one of its halls of residence is alive and responding to treatment, dismissing reports that he had died. The university, in an official statement signed by Johnson B. Akintayo, AVP, Communication, Media and Branding, said the student was receiving medical attention at the Babcock University Teaching Hospital. Official Statement: Update on the Hall Incident Babcock University confirms that the student involved is alive, responding well to treatment, and receiving the necessary medical care. His parents are on campus with him. Please read the full statement attached. pic.twitter.com/xsMQhWcA2z — Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Nigeria (@Babcock_Univ) November 9, 2026 “Contrary to reports suggesting that the student may have died, we wish to assure the public that he is responding positively to treatment and is receiving the necessary medical care,” the statement said. The incident occurred at one of the university’s student residential facilities. According to the institution, the situation was brought under control through the prompt intervention of the student’s roommates, whose actions prevented a potentially worse outcome. The university also disclosed that one of the students who participated in the rescue sustained injuries and was immediately taken for medical attention. It said the injured student’s parents had been contacted and were on campus to support their son as he received treatment. “The other student who sustained injury while rescuing his roommate, has been treated and discharged,” the statement added. Babcock University said it had commenced an investigation to establish the immediate and underlying circumstances surrounding the incident. The investigation, it explained, would help determine what happened, identify possible contributing factors and establish measures to prevent a recurrence. The institution also urged members of the public and media organisations to avoid spreading unverified information or attributing causes to the incident while investigations were ongoing. Beyond medical treatment, the university said it was committed to supporting the student’s recovery and well-being. “Babcock University takes the safety, health and welfare of its students and employees seriously,” the statement said. The institution further commended the student’s roommates for their courage and swift intervention, while appealing for sensitivity and restraint in discussions about the incident. It added that it would continue to monitor the student’s recovery and take necessary steps to establish the facts surrounding the incident. nigeria.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Rivers and Delta actually show
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Rivers and Delta states, neighbours in the South-South, backed different presidential candidates in the February 25, 2023 election, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Rivers, while Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, won Delta. Rivers: Tinubu ahead by 56,520 votes Tinubu polled 231,591 votes in Rivers, ahead of Obi’s 175,071. That put the APC candidate 56,520 votes clear of the runner-up. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, came third with 88,468 votes. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, trailed with 1,322. Delta: Obi’s commanding lead Delta produced the wider margin. Obi scored 341,866 votes, against 161,600 for Atiku, a lead of 180,266 votes. Tinubu managed 90,183 votes in Delta and finished third. Kwankwaso had 3,122. What the two results show together Taken together, the states reverse each other’s order. Tinubu won Rivers but placed third in Delta, while Obi won Delta and was runner-up in Rivers. Obi was the only candidate to finish in the top two in both states. The combined figures tell a different story from the two state winners alone. Obi polled 516,937 votes across Rivers and Delta, compared with Tinubu’s 321,774. This is a difference of 195,163 votes in Obi’s favour, even though Tinubu took the state with the higher turnout of the two. Obi’s vote in Delta alone, at 341,866, exceeded Tinubu’s combined total for both states by 20,092 votes. Atiku polled 250,068 votes across the two states, finishing third in Rivers and second in Delta. Kwankwaso placed fourth in both, with 4,444 votes combined. Tinubu’s support was uneven. He polled 231,591 votes in Rivers but only 90,183 in Delta, a drop of 141,408 votes between the two neighbouring states. nigeria.title: COP31: WMO warns El Niño could push 2027 temperatures higher
nigeria.description: The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned that 2027 could become the hottest year on record as an unusually strong El Niño combines with the effects of climate change to push global temperatures higher. WMO Secretary-General, Celeste Saulo, gave the warning on Monday while presenting the organisation’s State of the Climate Update 2026 at a news conference during the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye. Saulo said the past 12 years had been the warmest on record, with the last four years, including 2026, ranking as the hottest. She disclosed that global average temperatures between January and September 2026 were approximately 1.47 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. According to her, the developing 2026/2027 El Niño is unusually strong, with sea-surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific expected to approach four times the 0.5-degree threshold used to declare the climate phenomenon. “Indeed, this 2026/2027 El Niño is off the charts. It is different from any El Niño that we have monitored,” she said. The WMO chief explained that El Niño typically has its greatest impact on global temperatures in the following year, raising concerns that 2027 could surpass previous temperature records. She also revealed that ocean heat content had reached a record high for the 10th consecutive year, while global sea levels had risen to unprecedented levels, exposing about 900 million people living in low-lying coastal areas to increasing risks. Saulo warned that extreme heat, tropical cyclones and intense rainstorms were becoming more severe, exposing millions of people to dangerous weather conditions in 2026. She cited heatwaves across India, Pakistan, other parts of Asia and North America, as well as tens of thousands of excess deaths recorded in Europe. “The human and economic cost is unacceptably high,” she said. Saulo called on governments participating in COP31 to strengthen global climate observation systems and increase funding for early-warning mechanisms. She noted that the number of countries reporting multi-hazard early-warning systems had increased from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025. “We cannot afford to fly blind,” she said, emphasising the need for sustained climate monitoring to anticipate extreme weather events and protect vulnerable populations. Also speaking, the UN Climate Change Executive Secretary, Simon Stiell, described the climate crisis as a global health emergency, warning that extreme heat, pollution and climate-related disasters were placing increasing pressure on healthcare systems. Stiell said heatwaves during the northern hemisphere’s summer had killed an estimated 50,000 people across Europe, while hundreds of millions of people in southern Asia were exposed to extreme heat. “The climate crisis is now a global health crisis of pandemic proportions,” he said. nigeria.title: Full list: Messi makes FIFPRO World 11 as Ronaldo misses out
nigeria.description: Lionel Messi has been named in the 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11, extending his record as the most-selected player in the award’s history, while Cristiano Ronaldo failed to make the final team. Messi returns to the prestigious team for the first time since 2023, taking his record number of appearances to 18. The Argentine first made the selection in 2007 and has continued to earn recognition from fellow professional footballers across successive generations. Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal also made history after becoming the first player to earn two FIFPRO World 11 selections before turning 20. The Spain international was also included in last year’s team. Yamal joins fellow Spanish players David Raya, Pau Cubarsi and Rodri in the 2026 selection, taking Spain’s record tally of Men’s World 11 appearances to 53. The team was unveiled following votes from 19,806 professional male footballers across 73 countries, making it one of the few major football awards decided exclusively by players. Since 2005, FIFPRO has invited professional footballers worldwide to vote for the players they believe have delivered the most impressive performances during the assessment period. 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11 Goalkeeper David Raya (Arsenal, Spain) Defenders Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona, Spain) Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain, Morocco) Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Midfielders Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid, England) Rodri (Manchester City/Barcelona, Spain) Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Forwards Erling Haaland (Manchester City, Norway) Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid, France) Lionel Messi (Inter Miami, Argentina) Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, Spain) How the voting worked Professional footballers cast their votes through a secure digital platform provided by FIFPRO and its affiliated player unions. For the 2026 edition, players were assessed based on their performances between August 4, 2025, and July 19, 2026. nigeria.title: Ethiopian Airlines, Air Peace sign interline agreement to boost connectivity
nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Africa’s leading aviation group, Ethiopian Airlines, and Nigeria’s leading carrier, Air Peace, have signed a bilateral interline agreement, strengthening air transport connectivity across Africa and expanding travel opportunities for passengers. The partnership enables each airline to issue tickets for eligible itineraries that include flights operated by both carriers, providing customers with a more convenient and integrated travel experience. Through this collaboration, passengers will be able to book qualifying journeys on a single ticket and enjoy through-checked baggage to their destination, where applicable. Commenting on the partnership, Ethiopian Airlines Group Mr Mesfin Tasew, said “We are delighted to partner with Air Peace, a leading carrier in Nigeria, through this strategic interline agreement. This collaboration reflects our shared commitment to enhancing connectivity, improving customer convenience, and supporting the growth of air travel across the African continent. By combining our strengths, we are creating more travel opportunities and bringing Africa closer to the world.” For his part, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Air Peace, Allen Onyema, said: “This partnership with Ethiopian Airlines represents another significant milestone in our commitment to strengthening Africa’s aviation connectivity and bringing the continent closer together. By combining Air Peace’s extensive domestic, regional network, and our growing international network with Ethiopian Airlines’ global reach, we are creating greater opportunities for seamless travel in and out of the African continent. Beyond expanding travel options, this collaboration reflects our shared vision of fostering stronger economic, commercial and cultural ties across Africa and beyond. At Air Peace, we remain committed to building strategic partnerships that enhance passenger convenience, broaden connectivity and position African aviation as a formidable force in global air transport.” Meanwhile, the streamlined process eliminates the need for separate bookings and baggage re-checks, creating a smoother and more efficient travel experience. The agreement links Air Peace’s domestic and regional network with Ethiopian Airlines’ vast international network spanning Africa, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas. As a result, travellers departing from major Nigerian and west African cities will gain seamless access to Ethiopian Airlines’ global destinations through Addis Ababa, while international passengers arriving on Ethiopian Airlines flights will benefit from expanded onward travel options across Nigeria and west africa through Air Peace’s domestic network. nigeria.title: Toluwanisings laid to rest in Ibadan
nigeria.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has been laid to rest at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State, bringing an end to weeks of disagreement among members of his family over his final resting place. The gospel artiste was buried on Monday, November 9, 2026, in a private ceremony attended by family members following a funeral service at Banjola Event and Conference Centre, Alakia, Ibadan. His burial came after a disagreement between his widow, Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola, and his paternal relatives over where his remains should be interred. While his paternal family had expressed concerns about the circumstances surrounding his death and initially pushed for his burial in Ikirun, Osun State, his widow and associates were involved in discussions over the final arrangements. The disagreement attracted public attention and eventually prompted the intervention of the Oyo State Police Command. On November 3, the parties involved signed a peace undertaking at the police command headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, agreeing to avoid further public exchanges and actions capable of escalating tensions. Speaking on the agreement, the police command stated that, “All parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace.” The intervention paved the way for the family to settle on burying the singer at his Ibadan residence, where his wife and children live. Toluwanisings, who was widely recognised for his energetic worship ministrations and gospel songs, including A Very Big God, died on October 14, 2026. His death generated reactions across the gospel music community, while the disagreement surrounding his burial further drew public attention to the family’s situation. According to the Commission, the political stability of the nation will depend not only on how efficiently it conducts elections, but equally on how courageously, transparently and justly the judiciary adjudicates the disputes that follow. Describing the workshop’s theme, “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability,” as apt, the INEC Chairman stressed that, with the general election scheduled to commence on January 16, 2027, the Commission recognises that the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests upon impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He said: “While INEC manages the ballot, deploys technology, and safeguards the voter franchise, the Election Petition Tribunals stand as the ultimate guardians of democratic legitimacy. “When political contestations overflow from polling units into the courtroom, the Judiciary provides the constitutional sanctuary where grievances are transformed into peace, unlawful shortcuts are corrected, and the sovereign choice of the electorate is vindicated under the Rule of Law. “The credibility of elections cannot be measured solely by the conduct of voting or the declaration of results. nigeria.title: Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Political economist Pat Utomi has accused the APC-led government of abandoning its responsibilities while Nigerians pay out of pocket for basic services, from electricity and water to roads, healthcare and education. In a post on his X handle on Monday, Utomi questioned what citizens receive in return for paying taxes when households and communities must fund services that government is expected to provide. “The only thing this APC-led government is good at doing is making your life worse,” he wrote. Utomi said Nigerians buy generators to cope with unreliable electricity, sink boreholes for water and contribute money to repair roads. He also cited private security, healthcare and schools as costs families increasingly bear because public institutions have been neglected. He added that waste disposal, drainage, streetlights and transformers had also become private financial responsibilities. “Then what exactly are we paying this APC-led government to do?” he asked, arguing that governments elsewhere invest public resources in education, healthcare, infrastructure and social welfare. Utomi also criticised the government’s appeals for patience and sacrifice amid economic hardship. He cited the removal of petrol subsidies and increases in electricity tariffs and university fees, alongside rising healthcare costs. “But how much more must the people sacrifice while those in power continue to enjoy the privileges of office?” he asked. Utomi argued that taxation obliges government to provide public services, describing it as more than a contribution from citizens to politicians. “The government cannot collect from the people, abandon its responsibilities and then demand applause from the people they’re making their lives difficult,” he wrote. He concluded with a challenge to the government: “If Nigerians must finance their own survival, what exactly is the purpose of government?” In a separate post on Sunday, Utomi said the APC government had made the daily struggle to earn a living an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. He described the hardship as a tragedy for a richly endowed nation that he believes is poorly governed. He said: “The incompetence of the APC government has turned the daily struggle for survival into an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. Those who labour honestly to earn a living are being punished by a system that should be making their lives easier. What a tragedy for a nation so richly endowed yet so poorly governed!” The post Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. The issue is whether exchanges and other platforms can offer yield or rewards to investors who keep dollar-pegged stablecoins on their platforms. Seiberg views action as unlikely, though he sees a “narrow path” for a ban. His rationale is procedural as much as political: it may be easier to find 60 Senate votes on stablecoin yield alone than on the broader crypto market structure bill, which failed a cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and which he already called effectively dead for this Congress after the Democratic midterm sweep. A ban, he wrote, would benefit banks. He expects them to renew the push in the next Congress on the theory that Democratic wins open a path. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT Large bitcoin holders are swapping coins they guard themselves for shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) at a record pace, the firm’s head of digital assets said Monday, as kidnappings and hacks push security to the top of their list. “The current moment is the highest we’ve seen at any point,” Robbie Mitchnick told Barron’s , adding that demand for the swaps “has sort of been one way — up.” Of all the reasons clients give, he said, “the single largest one is security and peace of mind.” The trades are in-kind conversions. A holder delivers bitcoin to the fund through an intermediary and receives newly created IBIT shares, without first selling the coins for cash. BlackRock relies on Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to handle the transactions, and those firms set the minimum size. Barron’s put the volume BlackRock has seen at $3.6 billion, noting the real figure could be larger because the firm does not process every conversion itself. Mitchnick cited a bigger number in August, telling Bloomberg that IBIT had facilitated more than $5 billion of such swaps, up from more than $3 billion in October 2025 . In that August interview, BlackRock’s Mitchnick named the threats outright: “People see things happen in the outside world — whether it’s kidnappings, ransom, custody failures — that motivate them to make this switch for all or some of their holdings.” He told Barron’s the recent Binance hack was not news to big holders. “Most large Bitcoin holders were already acutely aware of the risk of holding on an exchange and in a hot wallet,” he said. How BlackRock’s swaps became possible The SEC voted on July 29, 2025, to let spot bitcoin and ether funds create and redeem shares in kind, ending the cash-only structure it required when the funds launched in January 2024. Access has widened since. BlackRock’s minimum started around $30 million and now hovers between $1 million and $2 million, Barron’s reported. Taxes are part of the pitch. Converting appreciated bitcoin into IBIT in kind “generally isn’t seen as a sale that would trigger capital-gains taxes,” Barron’s wrote, while Bloomberg cautioned that avoiding an immediate bill depends on the investor’s circumstances. Mitchnick also pointed to estate planning, calling it “much, much simpler” to hold the exposure “within the confines of their private bank.” Once inside, the coins sit with IBIT’s custodian, an affiliate of Coinbase Prime, in what Mitchnick called an “institutional-grade cold-storage model.” The fund held 795,921 BTC, worth about $60.4 billion, as of Nov. 6. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC Coinbase has won a full national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, upgrading the conditional approval it received in April and putting its institutional custody business under direct federal supervision, the exchange said Monday. The OCC approved the application for Coinbase National Trust Company last Friday, the company said in a blog post. OCC licensing records, as reported, show the chartering process was completed Nov. 6. Coinbase applied in October 2025 and received preliminary approval on April 2. In the intervening months it had to finish its organizational and operational preparations before the OCC would let the trust bank open. “This charter allows us to bring clear and consistent federal uniformity to our industry-leading custody capabilities,” Coinbase wrote, adding that it strengthens the regulatory framework under which it serves customers. The company said it has served as a custodian for more than 14 years. What the charter allows A national trust bank can hold assets for clients as a fiduciary, and Coinbase’s focus is custody for institutional customers. It is not a commercial bank. It cannot take ordinary retail deposits or make loans, and the charter does not authorize it to issue stablecoins. Staking, prime trading and financing will keep running through Coinbase affiliates, not the trust itself. Under the OCC’s April decision, the trust bank acts as an intermediary for those services and does not perform them directly. The decision also sets conditions. The trust bank must hold at least $60 million in Tier 1 capital and enough liquid assets to cover 180 days of operating expenses during its first three years. The license does not automatically connect Coinbase to Federal Reserve payment systems either. That requires a separate application under the Fed’s account access guidelines. Coinbase already runs custody through Coinbase Custody Trust Company, a limited-purpose trust regulated by the New York State Department of Financial Services. The company plans to move that business to the national entity over three years. A crowded charter queue Coinbase is the latest crypto firm to complete a federal trust charter. Ripple received final approval on Oct. 26, and Circle won final OCC approval in July, a decision that put USDC reserves on a path toward federal supervision. The OCC has been courting the sector. In August, Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould said “America and the OCC are once again open for business,” as the regulator touted its charter push. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. sports.title: 8 takeaways from the Bears' stressful win over the Buccaneers
sports.description: The victories seemed to be coming a little too easy for the Chicago Bears in recent weeks, so they made sure to put everyone through an extremely stressful one before heading off for their bye week. The Bears wrapped up their three-game prime-time tour with a home matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football and escaped with a 27-24 victory and improved to 7-2 on the season. Early on, however, it felt as if the game would be a blowout. Quarterback Caleb Williams quickly led two scoring drives to put the Bears up 14-0, with Tampa seemingly having no answers on either side of the ball. Everything was looking great, but then Williams began turning the ball over, something that is rare for him. Williams threw a career-high four interceptions on the day, and the Bears had five turnovers on the day. The offense couldn't muster any momentum, putting all the pressure on the Bears defense, which came through multiple times. The defense couldn't hold their ground forever, though. Eventually, those offensive miscues helped Tampa get back into the game as the Bears blew a 24-13 lead early in the fourth quarter to be tied 24-24 with just under two minutes to play. Fortunately, Williams responded by putting together one last scoring drive, complete with a big 38-yard completion to Colston Loveland to put the Bears in field goal range. Cairo Santos drilled a game-winning kick as everyone collectively exhaled. This will be one of the more memorable wins for all the wrong reasons, but it's still a win that keeps the Bears near the top of the playoff picture. Here are our takeaways from Sunday's stressful victory: 1. This is the reincarnation of 2006's Miracle in the Desert 20 years ago, Bears fans were treated to one of the most improbable and ugly wins in a special season. That, of course, was the "Miracle in the Desert" comeback win against the Arizona Cardinals, where the Bears committed six turnovers and needed big plays from the defense and special teams to get back in the game. And though this game may not have had the same comeback theatrics, it was every bit as gross and gritty to keep the winning streak alive. For nearly three full quarters, the offense didn't do much of anything and needed to rely on big plays by the defense to pick up the slack. It was ugly, and everything that could go wrong did go wrong. But the Bears never gave up and dug deep to get this victory. And great teams need to do that every once in a while. The Miracle in the Desert proved to everyone in the locker room that they have what it takes to win, no matter what happens. And that mindset helped propel them to Super Bowl XLI. Hopefully this will do the same, especially since it's the first time the Bears have won a game with a -3 turnover differential since then. We'll look back on this game with fond memories when the Bears are gunning for a title. 2. Caleb Williams had his worst game in 2 years This was a game we've quite literally never seen from Williams.

sports.title: Giants get great news on Cam Skattebo as fan favorite RB should be ‘full go’ in Week 10
sports.description: Giants get great news on Cam Skattebo as fan favorite RB should be ‘full go’ in Week 10 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Giants beat the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9, and they did so without their top two running backs. Cam Skattebo was out due to a hamstring injury, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve. Devin Singletary led the backfield, but it wasn't a very productive day on the ground. Getting Skattebo back as soon as possible is a must for this Giants' offense to function. They could trade for an RB as well, but Skattebo returning is the easiest way to improve. Fortunately, John Harbaugh told reporters, including Pat Leonard of NY Daily News Sports , that Skattebo should be a "full go" for the team in Week 10 when they face the Washington Commanders on Thursday Night Football. Giants expecting to get Cam Skattebo back for TNF "John Harbaugh says Cam Skattebo (hamstring) should be 'full go' Thursday night vs. the Washington Commanders," Leonard reports. "He was close to being able to play vs. the Eagles, but they were careful with him." This is a very encouraging update for the Giants on their fan favorite running back. While Skattebo didn't suit up in Week 9, he reportedly was close to playing. But with the Eagles being one of the worst teams in the NFL since Jalen Hurts was lost for the season, it made sense for the Giants to give Skattebo an extra week of rest. They had the ability to win without him, and did. MORE : Eagles’ Braden Mann boots punt not seen in over 20 years For Week 10, however, facing the Commanders and Jayden Daniels, having a good ground game will be huge. They could trade for Jonathan Taylor or another running back before the trade deadline, but they're set to get Skattebo back this week. Despite the fact that the Giants are playing the Commanders on Thursday Night Football, a short week, Skattebo is set to return for New York, providing a big boost to the offense. This is some great news for the Giants, as relying on the backfield they trotted out in Philadelphia is a recipe for disaster against more competitive teams. Skattebo is set to return and be a "full go" for the Giants on Thursday Night Football. It's some great news for the Giants, as they try to get to 6-2-1 and further separate themselves from the pack in the NFC East race. sports.title: Dan Campbell Has Complicated Decision to Make Before Germany Game
sports.description: The Detroit Lions improved to 6-2 with Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins, but head coach Dan Campbell now has an interesting decision to make regarding his offensive line. And based on what happened in Miami, it might be a decision that is easier to make on paper than in the locker room. Christian Mahogany was surprisingly benched for violating team rules, opening the door for second-year offensive lineman Miles Frazier to make his first NFL start at left guard. Unfortunately for Detroit, the results weren’t exactly encouraging. Campbell has built his program around accountability, and that’s not something he should abandon. However, with the Lions preparing for another important matchup against the New England Patriots, the question becomes whether Mahogany has already served his punishment or whether Campbell intends to make a longer-term change. His 48.8 pass-blocking grade and team-worst 37.8 run-blocking grade certainly won’t help his argument for remaining in the starting lineup. Frazier played all 59 offensive snaps against Miami, while Mahogany played exclusively on special teams. The Lions also struggled offensively, producing a season-low 270 total yards while Jared Goff was sacked three times. Of course, it would be unfair to blame Detroit’s offensive struggles entirely on Frazier. The offensive line had multiple issues, and Frazier did appear to settle down as the game progressed. However, the numbers make one thing clear: Frazier did not do enough in his first start to make the decision at left guard an obvious one. Dan Campbell Must Balance Discipline With Winning Following Sunday’s victory, Campbell made it clear that Mahogany’s benching was related to team rules rather than simply his performance on the field. The Lions have not publicly revealed what rule Mahogany violated, so judging the severity of the punishment would be premature. sports.title: ‘There was some deli meat given out’: Tom Brady takes jab at Drake Maye
sports.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Tom Brady returned to Foxboro this weekend for Rob Gronkowski’s New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction Saturday and Sunday’s game between the Pats and the Green Bay Packers. The former event went swimmingly for New England fans; the latter less so. Led by Jordan Love’s 372 passing yards and four total touchdowns, the Packers routed the Patriots 45-27. Drake Maye, New England’s third-year quarterback, had his share of struggles, tossing three critical interceptions. After the game, Brady the broadcaster had some fun at Maye’s expense during FOX’s postgame interviews. Drake throwing ‘deli meat’ Speaking with Green Bay Packers safety Evan Williams (five tackles, one interception), Brady noted that Maye was being generous with his passes throughout the game. “Xavier [McKinney] had two picks, you had one on the sideline. There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today,” Brady said . “I’m not gonna say that,” Williams responded, laughing, “but he was giving us some gifts for sure.” “There was a few out there, and you made him pay,” Brady added. Tom Brady took a dig at Drake Maye while interviewing #Packers S Evan Williams: “There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today.” ( @NFLonFOX) https://t.co/qp4SfQj1qP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 9, 2026 If you’re unfamiliar, Brady’s “deli meat” reference is a nod to Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake, who said last week that struggling Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was “throwing deli meat out there” in a loss to the Rams. Lake later apologized to Herbert via text message, claiming he wasn’t trying to be “disrespectful.” Back to Brady We’re guessing Brady wasn’t trying to be cruel toward Maye with his postgame barb, even if his assessment was harsh (though not unfair). After throwing only four touchdowns and seven interceptions in his first four games, Maye tossed 11 TDs and only one pick his next four before Sunday’s ugly showing. “We haven’t had a clean, a turnover-free game yet. It’s, starting with me, it’s one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games,” Maye said after yesterday’s loss. “I’d say, put our defense in a bad spot in the first, the first drive, and just gave them the football and had some other chances down the field and got to see in front. I got to see in front. I feel like I was just a little late sometimes. I feel like we got into a throwing game, and that’s partly because of what we did offensively, and then we didn’t really get to build off the run game, and I think we just got to start the game, and me specifically, start better.” New England is back in action this Sunday when they take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany. sports.title: No room for Kane! Messi back in FIFPRO XI as Yamal breaks teenage record
sports.description: Inter Miami CF v Charlotte FC - Getty Images Sport The 2026 FIFPRO Men's World 11 has been officially announced, featuring a mix of legendary veterans and record-breaking youngsters. However, the selection has sparked debate following the high-profile exclusion of Harry Kane, despite the England striker holding the 2026 Ballon d'Or. Messi returns as Yamal makes history Lionel Messi has secured his place in the FIFPRO Men's World 11 once again, marking a triumphant return to the elite lineup for the first time since 2023. His comeback follows a stellar international campaign where he scored eight goals to lead Argentina to the World Cup final, which they narrowly lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time. Joining him in the history books is Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, who continues to shatter expectations . The Spanish international has become the first player ever to be selected for the World 11 twice before reaching the age of 20. He is one of four Spanish players included in this season's lineup, alongside David Raya, Pau Cubarsi, and Rodri Hernandez. Shock omission for Harry Kane The biggest talking point of the announcement is undoubtedly the absence of Kane. Despite the England captain being the reigning Ballon d'Or winner , he failed to garner enough votes from his fellow professionals to make the final cut. Kane's exclusion highlights the intense competition for attacking spots, with voters clearly favouring a standout frontline. Erling Haaland secured his place after finishing as the Premier League top scorer last season with 27 goals, while also scoring seven times to lead Norway to their first-ever World Cup quarter-final. Alongside him, Kylian Mbappe earned his spot after bagging 10 goals to finish as the World Cup top scorer, officially becoming the tournament's all-time leading goalscorer. Ligue 1 and PSG dominance Paris Saint-Germain enjoyed a strong showing in the final XI, with the French champions boasting three representatives in the squad following their back-to-back Champions League titles. The defensive unit features Moroccan star Achraf Hakimi and Portuguese left-back Nuno Mendes, alongside midfielder Vitinha, all rewarded for their pivotal roles in the club's European success. The lineup was selected following a vote by 19,806 professional footballers across 73 countries. Eligible players were evaluated on their performances between August 4, 2025, and July 19, 2026, provided they featured in at least 30 official matches during that period. The complete 2026 FIFPro World 11 The complete 2026 FIFPro World 11 lineup features Raya in goal, behind a backline of Hakimi, Cubarsi, and Mendes. The midfield trio consists of Rodri, Vitinha, and Jude Bellingham, while Messi, Yamal, Mbappe, and Haaland form a formidable frontline. sports.description: After recording 18 rushing yards on 17 carries against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the New Orleans Saints entered the bye week searching for answers to their struggling run game. On Nov. 2, the Saints announced the firing of run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti and tasked offensive line coach Brendan Nugent with leading the run game. Nugent already played a significant role in preparing the rushing attack. What does Paganetti’s firing fix for the Saints going forward? From Super Bowl Champ To Unemployed From 2023 to 2024 in Philadelphia, Paganetti was the run game specialist. In 2024, the Eagles ranked second in rushing with 3,048 yards . Philadelphia went on to win Super Bowl LIX and averaged 204.5 rushing yards across their four playoff games. After winning the Super Bowl with Moore, the Saints hired him as their run game coordinator. In 2025, New Orleans finished 28th in rushing yards per game and 31st in yards per carry. In his seven games as coordinator in 2026 , the Saints remained 28th in rushing yards per game and ranked 30th in yards per carry, with their average dropping from 3.7 to 3.5. After the firing, Paganetti’s brother Ryan claimed in a now-deleted X post that Paganetti’s role was more of a support role rather than installing and implementing run techniques. sports.title: When is the NFL trade deadline? See which Eagles might get traded
sports.description: For the first time in years, the Philadelphia Eagles find themselves in a rare position as likely sellers as the NFL trade deadline nears. In what experts predicted would be a possible Super Bowl run and at the very least a third straight NFC East Division title, the Birds are currently at the bottom of the division and with one of the worst records in the league at 2-7. Much of the blame can be blamed on injuries up and down the roster with the main blow coming after quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the season due to blood clots in his lungs. Losing future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson to retirement hurt just as much. But inconsistent play calling from both sides of the ball haven't helped either as new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion's system has been a dud halfway through the season. technology.title: Machine learning researchers build a better world model
technology.description: Machine learning researchers have developed a technique that allows world models to make better predictions about how objects will behave. World models are used to train physical AI systems like robots how to navigate the real world. They predict the consequences of actions. But they do so based on observed data. These models could provide better direction to robots if they were able to make inferences about possible actions without being trained for all the possible outcomes. Randall Balestriero (Brown University, AMI Labs), Kerda Varaku, and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun (NYU, AMI Labs) describe an approach that might allow that to happen in a pre-print paper, "Counterfactual World Models: Natura Non Facit Saltus." The Latin refers to Gottfried Leibniz's axiom " nature makes no leaps ," which had a good run until it ran headlong into quantum mechanics. Yet for the authors, the saying explains how they have been able to devise a method for zero-shot physics inference. Counterfactual world models, said Balestriero in an email to The Register use "the mismatch between your prediction and the real world to figure out what did you get wrong, and from that you can better understand what happened for better future predictions, debugging, reasoning, all at test time." Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture ( JEPA ) models, developed by LeCunn and colleagues back in 2023, have been proposed for robots because they can take an action as input and ask what the world would be like with that action. But a JEPA world model produces an average of outcomes and would not be able to anticipate counterfactual scenarios – events that didn't happen. The technique that the researchers developed is not specific to JEPAs – it can be applied to any world model that predicts the average next state under any action. But JEPA models are particularly well suited to being adapted. Balestriero said that the counterfactual world model experiments were done using off-the-shelf encoders (DINOv2 and MAE) without any fine-tuning and only a small predictor trained on top. Creating a counterfactual world model from that starting point would only require minor additions. Counterfactual world models predict alternative scenarios more effectively by inferring possibilities from what did occur. "In causal inference, answering 'What would have happened had I acted differently?' takes three steps," explained Balestriero. "You use what you observed to learn something about those hidden factors, you change the action, and you predict again with the hidden factors kept exactly as they were. "Our counterfactual world model does all three steps with one subtraction." Balestriero cited an example from the paper: a boat crossing a river with a hidden current and how the JEPA world model and counterfactual world model predicted the boat's movements. "The world model predicted where the boat would end up after steering left, and it actually ended up two meters further downstream," he explained.
